summary: A compact Chinatown temple visit built around an extraordinary object: the approximately three-metre, 5.5-tonne Golden Buddha. Its concealed-under-plaster history gives the visit more interest than another ornate shrine alone. Shortlist it as an easy cultural stop alongside Yaowarat or Talat Noi; allow extra time for the separately ticketed Chinatown heritage exhibition if open.
whyGo: See the actual Golden Buddha in an elevated shrine hall rather than a replica.
The lower-floor exhibitions add context on the statue and Bangkok’s Chinese community.
A convenient starting point for exploring Chinatown without committing half a day.
bestFor: First-time Bangkok visitors interested in Buddhist art
History-minded travellers combining temples and Chinatown
A short cultural stop before a neighbourhood walk
skipIf: You have temple fatigue and little interest in the statue’s story
You want extensive peaceful grounds or a long immersive attraction
Stairs are a barrier and you cannot confirm an accessible route
duration: Plan 30–45 minutes for the shrine; allow around 60–90 minutes with exhibitions. These are planning estimates.
cost: Budget at least THB 100 per adult for the main visit, as listed by Tourism Authority of Thailand Japan. Other current guides quote THB 40 for the shrine and THB 100 separately for the heritage exhibition; ticket scope and current charges need confirmation at the desk.
hours: Tourism Authority of Thailand Japan lists 08:00–17:00 daily. Exhibition hours can differ; secondary listings report a Monday closure for the heritage exhibition.
bestTime: At opening for a cooler walk and a better chance of fewer tour groups. Afternoon works before Chinatown dinner, provided you arrive well before closing.
gettingThere: MRT Blue Line to Hua Lamphong (BL28), then approximately 10 minutes on foot to Thanon Mittaphap Thai-China, near the eastern entrance to Yaowarat. Pavements and road crossings can be busy.
booking: Ordinary independent visits appear to use on-site admission; no advance reservation requirement was identified. A guide is optional. Bring baht for tickets.
accessibility: The Buddha occupies the top floor of a multi-storey pavilion with prominent stairs. A reliable current visitor lift policy and step-free route were not verified; check directly before relying on wheelchair access.
practicalTips: Cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where indicated before entering the shrine.
This is an active place of worship: keep voices low and avoid pointing feet towards the Buddha.
Visit the temple before walking onward to Chinatown; evening street-food activity begins after normal temple hours.
decemberNotes: December is a practical month for combining the shrine with outdoor Chinatown exploration, although midday can still feel hot. Peak-season queues are possible. No December 2026 special opening schedule or ceremony-related closure calendar was verified; check close to your chosen date.
uncertainties: Official ticket scope conflicts with secondary price listings; museum admission may be additional.
Museum Monday closure and exact exhibition hours lack current primary confirmation.
Current lift access, photography restrictions and December closures are unconfirmed.
